I can’t compute the requested cluster assignments, updated modes, silhouettes, or silhouette plot from the information given because the actual data table is missing.

To solve the problem numerically, I need the seven rows, e.g.

\[
x_i=(\text{township}_i,\ \text{four-bedrooms}_i,\ \text{style}_i),\qquad i=1,\dots,7,
\]

and I also need to know which two houses are chosen as the initial K-modes.

---

What the solution would require:

For houses \(i,j\), the K-modes dissimilarity is

\[
d(i,j)
=
\mathbf 1\{\text{township}_i\ne \text{township}_j\}
+
\mathbf 1\{\text{four-bedrooms}_i\ne \text{four-bedrooms}_j\}
+
\mathbf 1\{\text{style}_i\ne \text{style}_j\}.
\]

### (a) Cluster assignment and updated modes

Given initial modes \(m_1,m_2\), assign each house \(i\) to the closer mode:

\[
i\in C_1 \quad \text{if}\quad d(x_i,m_1)\le d(x_i,m_2),
\]

and otherwise \(i\in C_2\), with some specified tie-breaking rule if distances are equal.

The updated mode for each cluster is computed coordinatewise by taking the most frequent category in that cluster. For example,

\[
\widehat m_{1,\text{township}}
=
\text{most frequent township among houses in } C_1.
\]

The same is done for the four-bedroom variable and the style variable.

### (b) Silhouette values

For house \(i\), let \(C(i)\) be its assigned cluster.

The within-cluster average dissimilarity is

\[
a(i)
=
\frac{1}{|C(i)|-1}
\sum_{\substack{j\in C(i)\\j\ne i}} d(i,j).
\]

Since there are only two clusters, the between-cluster average dissimilarity is simply

\[
b(i)
=
\frac{1}{|C'|}
\sum_{j\in C'} d(i,j),
\]

where \(C'\) is the other cluster.

Then

\[
s(i)
=
\frac{b(i)-a(i)}{\max\{a(i),b(i)\}}.
\]

A value near \(1\) means the house is well matched to its cluster; a value near \(0\) means it lies between clusters; a negative value means it may be assigned to the wrong cluster.

### (c) Silhouette plot and interpretation

The silhouette plot would display the seven \(s(i)\) values as horizontal bars, grouped by cluster and usually sorted from largest to smallest within each cluster.

The clustering is considered well-structured if most silhouette values are large and positive, say close to \(1\). It is weak or poorly structured if many values are near \(0\) or negative.

---

Please provide the table of the seven houses and the two initial modes, and I can compute the full numerical solution.
